title: OpenAPI and Swagger: specification and living documentation

videos.script: Everything a client of shelf needs to know is written somewhere already. It is written in Python, inside rest.py. {{code}} Nobody calling your API should have to read your code to use it. This lesson writes the contract down instead, in a format called OpenAPI. Every address, every method, every field and every status code, in one file. {{document}} People read that file as a page. Tools read it to draw that page, or to generate code. {{readers}} And a test reads it too. You write a short program that calls the running API and holds each answer up against the file. {{test}} On shelf, it finds two places where the code and its description disagree. One of them lets the same book into the shop twice. {{found}} That is what living documentation means here. A description that fails the day it stops being true. Then you use the file to catch a breaking change before it ships, and you weigh what generated code costs. {{uses}}
